heroHeadline: Trump Demands Iran Put Nuclear Concessions in Writing — SAVE Act Killed Again by Four GOP Senators; Bolton Pleads Guilty; Day 500 Schedule Policy/Career EO — Day 502
heroSubtitle: On June 5, 2026 (Day 502 of Trump's second term / Day 97 of the US-Iran war), ABC News reported Trump is demanding Iran put any nuclear concessions in writing before finalizing any deal — a day after softening his stance by declaring Iran's enriched uranium is 'entombed' and the US has 'no reason' to retrieve it. On June 4, the Senate blocked the SAVE America Act for a second time as four Republicans (Collins, McConnell, Murkowski, Tillis) joined all Democrats to kill the voter ID mandate; former National Security Adviser John Bolton agreed to plead guilty to retaining classified national security information with a $2.25 million restitution payment. On June 3 (Day 500), Trump signed two executive orders: 'Schedule Policy/Career' strips civil service protections from approximately 8,000 senior federal workers (GS-15 and above), and 'Strengthening Customs Enforcement' tightens duty evasion penalties; at a full Cabinet meeting, Trump declared Iran 'negotiating on fumes' and said midterms would not affect his war strategy as CENTCOM shot down 4 Iranian drones and struck an Iranian ground control station in Bandar Abbas. The State Department also announced it will reduce Africa visa processing from ~50 embassies to 20 regional hubs. Oil prices eased toward ~$88-93/bbl from the June 1 spike as back-channel Iran talks continued through intermediaries; US officials say Iran has provided verbal assurances on some nuclear issues but refused to put commitments in writing. Fed Chair Warsh hired Paul Winfree — described as having written the 'blueprint for taking the modern Federal Reserve apart' — ahead of Warsh's first FOMC meeting as Chair on June 16-17.
